tests.title: The reader splits well-formed frontmatter from the body, and reads a file without frontmatter whole
given: a steering file with frontmatter holding a version and two amendments, and the same directives with no frontmatter at all
tests.when: the steering is read from the spec root
then: with frontmatter, the body is the text after the closing delimiter and holds none of the frontmatter's bytes
the version is the frontmatter's version and the amendments are its two entries in file order, newest first
without frontmatter, the body is the file's bytes exactly as they are
without frontmatter, no version and no amendment is reported and no broken rule is named
tests.pseudocode: table in internal/project/steering_test.go, beside TestSteering_ReturnsTheDirectives: write the case's file into a temp spec root; s = project.ReadSteering(dir); assert s.Body == case.body; assert s.Version == case.version; assert s.Amendments == case.amendments; assert s.Problems is empty

tests.title: A well-formed record is accepted and each malformed shape names exactly the rule it breaks
given: a frontmatter that meets every well-formedness rule

one frontmatter per rule that breaks only that rule: an unknown key, no version, no amendments key, an empty amendment list, a version with a leading zero, a version with four numbers, an amendment with no date, an amendment with an empty change, a date that is not YYYY-MM-DD, two amendment versions that do not strictly decrease, two dates that increase, and a first amendment whose version is not the file's
one frontmatter that breaks three rules at once
then: the well-formed file is versioned and names no broken rule

each single-fault file names exactly one broken rule, and the rule named is the one it breaks: the rules are checked in the order they are listed, and a rule whose subject an earlier broken rule has rejected is not checked, so an absent version and an amendment with no version each name one rule and not two
the file that breaks three names all three, in a fixed order that is the same on every run
every malformed file still returns its body, and reports no version
tests.pseudocode: table in internal/project/steering_test.go, one case per rule: s = project.ReadSteering(dir); assert s.Problems == case.problems; assert s.Version == ""; assert s.Body == case.body

tests.title: A frontmatter delimiter that is never closed is malformed and the whole file is the body
given: a steering file that opens with a line of three hyphens and holds no closing delimiter
then: exactly one broken rule is named, saying the frontmatter has no closing delimiter
the body is the file's bytes as they are, the opening delimiter among them
no version and no amendment is reported
tests.pseudocode: in internal/project/steering_test.go: s = project.ReadSteering(dir); assert len(s.Problems) == 1 and it names the missing closing delimiter; assert s.Body == the whole file; assert s.Version == ""

tests.title: Two versions are compared as three integers, not as text
given: pairs of versions in the version form: 2.10.0 and 2.9.0, 1.0.1 and 1.0.0, 2.0.0 and 1.99.99, 1.0.0 and 1.0.0, and 0.0.0 and 0.0.1
then: 2.10.0 is newer than 2.9.0, which a text comparison would get wrong
1.0.1 is newer than 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 is newer than 1.99.99
1.0.0 and 1.0.0 compare equal
the comparison is antisymmetric: swapping the pair reverses the answer
tests.pseudocode: table in internal/project/steering_test.go: assert compare(case.a, case.b) == case.want and compare(case.b, case.a) == -case.want

tests.title: The body checks are made on the body after the frontmatter, and a file with nothing to say has no version
given: versioned files whose body in turn is empty, is only the placeholder marker, is only the bare heading, and is one byte over the 24 KB bound
a versioned file whose body is just within the bound and whose body and frontmatter together are over it
then: each of the first four reads as nothing: an empty body, no version and no amendment
the fifth is read in full, with its body and its version, because the bound is measured over the body alone
none of the five names a broken rule
tests.pseudocode: table in internal/project/steering_test.go, beside TestSteering_IgnoresAFileWithNothingToSay: build each body around maxSteeringBytes; s = project.ReadSteering(dir); assert s.Body == case.body and s.Version == case.version

tests.title: The steering block names the version when there is one, and is unchanged when there is not
given: directive text with a version, the same text with no version, and a steering with nothing to say
tests.when: the steering block of a phase prompt is built for each
then: with a version the block holds the line naming it before the body, between the heading and the BEGIN STEERING marker
the text between the BEGIN and END markers is the body alone, with none of the frontmatter's bytes
with no version the block is byte-identical to the one built from the same text before this change
with nothing to say the block is empty: no heading, no marker and no version line
tests.pseudocode: table in specgen/prompts_test.go, beside TestRunContextBlock: got = steeringBlock(case.body, case.version); assert got == case.want, the no-version case compared against the block this repository built before the change

tests.title: The amendment record reaches none of the prompts that are given the steering
given: a versioned steering whose amendments carry distinctive dates and change sentences that appear nowhere else
tests.when: the prompt is built for each phase that is handed the steering: the split decision, the requirements, test specification and tasks phases, the architecture phase and the PRD review
then: no prompt holds any amendment's date
no prompt holds any amendment's change sentence
every prompt does hold the directive text and the version line
tests.pseudocode: in specgen/phases_test.go, over the six prompt builders: for each prompt — assert !strings.Contains(prompt, amendment.Date) and !strings.Contains(prompt, amendment.Change) for every amendment; assert strings.Contains(prompt, directiveText)

tests.title: An optional steering_version round-trips through the PRD frontmatter in a fixed position
given: a prd.md whose frontmatter holds steering_version, and one whose frontmatter does not
tests.when: each package is loaded, saved and loaded again
then: the one with the field loads with its value and the save writes the same key with the same value
the key is written after schema_version and before owner
the one without the field loads without it and the save writes no steering_version key, neither empty nor null
both packages validate, and both round-trip byte-identically
tests.pseudocode: table in afspec/prd_test.go, beside the other frontmatter round-trip tests: s = LoadSpec(dir); assert s.SteeringVersion == case.want; Save(dir); assert the rendered prd.md lines between schema_version and owner; assert LoadSpec(dir) equals s; assert s.Validate().Valid

tests.title: A steering_version that is not in the version form is a schema error on prd.md
given: packages whose prd.md carries steering_version in turn as 2.1, 2.1.0.0, 02.1.0, v2.1.0, 2.1.x and 2.1.0-rc1, and one that carries it as the empty string
then: each of the six malformed values gives one error whose check is json_schema and whose artifact is prd.md
the error's path names steering_version, and the result is not valid
the empty value is read as the field being absent: no error is reported, the result is valid, and a save writes no steering_version key
tests.pseudocode: table in afspec/validate_test.go, beside TestValidate_ReportsAnUnknownKeyOnDisk: write the case's frontmatter; v = LoadSpec(dir).Validate(); assert v.Valid == case.valid; for the malformed cases assert one error with Check "json_schema", Artifact "prd.md" and "steering_version" in its Path; for the empty case assert no such error and that renderPRD omits the key

tests.title: Changing steering_version on an active package is accepted and leaves the intent hash alone
given: an active package with an intent hash and a steering_version of 1.0.0
tests.when: the field is changed to 2.0.0 and the package is saved, then loaded again
then: the save returns no error
the intent_hash in prd.md is the same before and after
no intent drift is reported for the package
the reloaded package carries the new value and still validates
tests.pseudocode: in afspec/afspec_test.go, beside TestSave_RefusesIntentDriftOnAnActiveSpec: s = LoadSpec(dir); before = *s.IntentHash; s.SteeringVersion = "2.0.0"; assert s.Save(dir) == nil; r = LoadSpec(dir); assert *r.IntentHash == before; assert !specpkg.IntentDrift(r); assert r.SteeringVersion == "2.0.0"

tests.title: A run writes the steering's version into the package, and leaves the field out when there is none
given: a run against a spec root whose steering is in turn versioned, unversioned, malformed, and a bare heading with nothing to say
tests.when: the pipeline builds and writes a package, once for a single scope and once for a split of two scopes
then: under a versioned steering every package written holds steering_version with the steering's version
under each of the other three no package holds a steering_version key at all
every package written validates in all four cases
tests.pseudocode: table in specgen/pipeline_test.go, beside the tests that read a written package's prd.md: run the pipeline against the scripted model; for each written package assert the frontmatter's steering_version is case.want or absent; assert the reported validation is valid

tests.title: A run against a malformed record warns once at preflight and runs every phase all the same
given: a spec root whose steering frontmatter breaks two rules, and a scripted model that answers every phase
then: exactly one warning with code steering_malformed and severity high is in the envelope, at stage preflight
its message names both broken rules
the warning is raised before the first model call
every phase is given the directive body, and the run's exit code is the one it would have had under an unversioned steering
tests.pseudocode: in specgen/pipeline_test.go, beside TestPipeline's preflight-warning cases: run the pipeline; ws = warnings(run, "steering_malformed"); assert len(ws) == 1 and ws[0].Severity == "high" and ws[0].Stage == "preflight"; assert the recorded prompts hold the directive body; assert the exit code matches the unversioned run

tests.title: speca --validate warns once about a malformed record and gives the verdict it would otherwise give
given: a spec root holding a valid package and a steering file whose frontmatter breaks one rule
tests.when: speca <package> --validate is run against it, and then again with the frontmatter removed
then: the first call carries exactly one high steering_malformed warning at stage preflight, naming the broken rule
the exit code is 0
result.valid and every entry of result.validation are the same in both calls
the report form, speca <package> without --validate, carries no such warning
tests.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/verdict_test.go, beside TestVerdict_WithAnUnreadableSpecRoot: code = Main(["--dir", root, ref, "--validate"], &out, &err); assert code == 0; env = decode(out); assert one warning steering_malformed, severity high, stage preflight; compare env.result.validation with the run against the frontmatter-free file

tests.title: The rule says nothing for an equal version and names the amendments a package missed
given: a spec root whose steering is at 2.1.0 with a record of 2.1.0, 2.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.0.0
draft and active packages whose steering_version is in turn 2.1.0, 2.0.0 and 1.1.0
tests.when: the verdict is taken on each package
then: at 2.1.0 no entry whose check is steering_version is reported
at 2.0.0 exactly one warning is reported, naming 2.0.0, 2.1.0 and the 2.1.0 amendment with its date and change, and nothing of the older amendments

at 1.1.0 the one warning names the 2.1.0 and 2.0.0 amendments, newest first, and also says that a directive the package was written under has been removed or changed, 2.0.0 having raised the MAJOR number
at 2.0.0, where no amendment since raised the MAJOR number, that sentence is absent
the entry's artifact is prd.md, and no second entry under the rule is reported in any case
tests.pseudocode: table in internal/specpkg/steering_test.go: write the steering into a temp spec root; v, err = specpkg.Verdict(specsDir, spec); assert err == nil; got = entries(v, "steering_version"); assert got matches case.want in count, severity and the substrings it must carry

tests.title: The rule says so when a package claims a version the steering has not reached or has never had
given: a spec root whose steering is at 2.0.0 with a record of 2.0.0 and 1.0.0
draft packages whose steering_version is in turn 3.0.0 and 1.5.0
tests.when: the verdict is taken on each package
then: at 3.0.0 one warning names both versions and says the package's version is newer than the steering's
at 1.5.0 one warning names both versions and says the version is in no amendment of the record
both entries have check steering_version and artifact prd.md
neither case reports a second entry under the rule
tests.pseudocode: table in internal/specpkg/steering_test.go: v, _ = specpkg.Verdict(specsDir, spec); got = entries(v, "steering_version"); assert len(got) == 1 and its message carries both versions and case.says

tests.title: The rule stays silent where it does not apply, and is never an error
given: a spec root whose steering is at 2.0.0
packages that differ from it in turn by being sealed, superseded or archived, by carrying no steering_version, and by sitting under a steering that is unversioned and under one that is malformed
tests.when: the verdict is taken on each
then: no entry whose check is steering_version is reported in any of the cases
across every case of this test and of TS-16-14 and TS-16-15, no error whose check is steering_version is ever reported
result.valid is decided by the other rules alone
tests.pseudocode: table in internal/specpkg/steering_test.go: for each case — v, _ = specpkg.Verdict(specsDir, spec); assert entries(v, "steering_version") is empty; and over every case assert no entry with that check is in v.Errors

tests.title: A maintainer amends the steering, reads what a package missed, and clears the warning
given: a real spec root holding an active package with steering_version 1.0.0 and a steering file at 1.0.0
tests.when: a directive and an amendment at 1.1.0 are added to the real steering file, speca <package> --validate is run, the field in prd.md is changed to 1.1.0, and the verdict is taken again
then: the first verdict carries one warning under the rule steering_version naming 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and the new amendment with its date and change
both verdicts exit 0 and report the package as valid
the second verdict carries no finding under the rule
nothing but prd.md changed in the package between the two calls
tests.pseudocode: end-to-end case in cmd/speca/e2e_test.go, beside TestAnAgentFollowsNextFromTheReportToTheFinishedTask: copy a fixture package and a versioned steering into a real temp spec root; v1 = decode(Main([ref, "--validate"])); assert the warning; rewrite the field in prd.md; v2 = decode(Main([ref, "--validate"])); assert no steering_version entry

the verdict over a real spec root
a real package directory on the file system

then: the run exits 0 and reports the package as valid
the written prd.md holds steering_version with the steering's version
the verdict the run reports carries no finding under the rule steering_version
the prompts the scripted model saw hold the version line and none of the amendment record

then: the run carries exactly one high steering_malformed warning at stage preflight, naming the broken rule
the run exits with the code it would have had under an unversioned steering, and the package is written and valid
the prompts the scripted model saw hold the directive body and no version line
the written prd.md holds no steering_version key
